text_extraction: react_review.retrieval.local_pdf._pdf_text — the same function the run uses. Offsets from any other extraction are offsets into a document nothing reads.
join_key: audit_ids, matched against a reading's claim_ids. Not (study, field, shape): that triple is not an identity — the same study reports the same field under several column labels, and each is its own batch with its own window.
why_v2: v1 assumed the three arm counts were read together. They are not: they come from three different review columns, the group key includes the raw field name, and each is its own batch with one claim. v1 described a reading that never happens, which the old (study, field, shape) join hid by collapsing all three into it. Every batch here was produced by eval/excerpt_dry_run.py from the real grouping.
purpose: Where the evidence for each batched claim actually is, so that a refusal caused by the window can be told from a refusal caused by the paper. A run cannot make this distinction: 'the paper does not report it' and 'the passage was never sent' are the same sentence from the extractor.
not_derived_from: audit_template.csv's `derivation` column, which records how a REVIEW CELL was split ('split trailing n from explicit arm cell') and says nothing about the paper. And not from `source_quote` alone: MA002's quote establishes an explicit total and cannot establish a partition, which is a different claim needing a different sentence.
scope: Batched routes only. Under phase8_batch the arm_identity route is targeted_v4, one call per claim, so treatment_arm rows (MA003, MA005, MA007) form no batch and are deliberately absent.

batches.why: A text field, to keep the set from being only numbers.
